findings.title: Journal requests have no timeout: a hung add or save leaves the button stuck on 'Saving…' forever
findings.where: Plant detail page journal form (POST /api/journal); edit-in-place (PUT /api/journal/{id})
findings.steps: Open /plants/1, make POST /api/journal hang (browser_route that never responds), type an entry, click 'Add entry', wait over 10 s.
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 seconds with a visible error, and the button becomes usable again, with the text kept.
findings.actual: After 12 s the button still reads 'Saving…' and stays disabled. There is no error and no way to cancel or retry without reloading.
findings.evidence: After 12 s, the submit button's innerText was 'Saving…'. useApiClient ($fetch.create) sets no timeout.

findings.title: Journal error states have no retry
findings.where: /journal page and the Journal section of /plants/{id}
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal* return 500, then open /journal through the nav link, or open a plant from the plants list. Then let the server recover.
findings.expected: The error message has a Retry button that reloads the entries in place.
findings.actual: Only 'Could not load the journal.' is shown, with no retry control. On the plant page, the only buttons in the section are 'Add entry' and the edit/delete buttons. To recover you must reload or change the search.
findings.evidence:
/journal main text: '...Search

Could not load the journal.' with no button. In the plant detail journal section: 'Entries, newest first
Could not load the journal.' with no retry button.

findings.title: Very large ids cause 500 Internal Server Error on the journal endpoints
findings.steps: curl POST /api/journal with {"plant_id":99999999999999999999,"entry_on":"2026-11-12","body":"x"}; or GET /api/journal?plant_id=99999999999999999999999; or PUT/DELETE /api/journal/99999999999999999999999
findings.actual: HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error'. SQLite overflows on an integer larger than 64 bits. No upper bound is validated.
findings.evidence: All four calls returned 'Internal Server Error 500'.

findings.title: A long plant name overflows the Journal page at 375 px
findings.steps: Create a plant named with 80 'W' characters (no spaces), add a journal entry to it, open /journal at a 375 px width.
findings.expected: No sideways scrolling; the plant name wraps.
findings.actual: document scrollWidth is 1568 px. The .journal-feed__plant link has no overflow-wrap and pushes the card wider than the screen. Entry bodies wrap correctly.
findings.evidence: scrollWidth 1568 at viewport 375. The widest element is a.journal-feed__plant (right edge 1551 px).

findings.title: Search longer than 80 characters shows a raw validation error instead of results
findings.steps: On /journal, type or paste 81 or more characters into Search.
findings.expected: The input limits the length, or the page shows a friendly reason.
findings.actual: The entries disappear and the page shows 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'. The input has no maxlength.
findings.evidence: Main text after typing 81 'a' characters: 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'.

findings.title: Retrying an add after a timeout or network failure can create a duplicate entry
findings.steps: Add an entry while the connection is slow, so the request reaches the server but the response is lost or the client gives up. Click 'Add entry' again.
findings.expected: One entry is created (for example, with an idempotency key or by de-duplicating).
findings.actual: Each POST inserts a new row with no idempotency key. A request I had held pending in the browser was still committed later (entry 'hang', id 7) even though the UI never confirmed it, so a retry would have made a second copy.
findings.evidence: After the hung-POST test, GET /api/journal listed the 'hang' entry, which the UI never showed as saved.

findings.title: The 'today' limit uses the server's local date while the form uses the browser's
findings.steps: As a user ahead of the server's time zone (e.g. UTC+10 against a UTC server), in the early morning add an entry dated the browser's today.
findings.actual: The server rejects it: 'Entry on: Journal date cannot be in the future.'
findings.evidence: Code: the backend compares against date.today() in the server's time zone, while the form's max is the client's local date.

findings.title: An entry edited within a second of being created is not marked 'edited'
findings.steps: Add an entry and edit it straight away (within the same second).
findings.actual: datetime('now') has 1-second resolution, so the timestamps match and the marker is hidden.
